items.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Where do you think Sleepy John is now? [INTERVIEWEE] Brown with Tennessee the last time I heard from him. He done went blind now.

ctx.x: Well, him and them recorded some records a while back. Around about 26 or 27, they made the record called The Diving Duck and The Brickish Jail. Something else they made, but I can't remember what else they made, but I know they made about two or three records.
Where do you think Sleepy John is now?
Brown with Tennessee the last time I heard from him. He done went blind now.

items.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25
items.q: The interviewee discusses Sleepy John Estes only in the context of Ham Lewis joining him and recording records; no direct personal interaction or relationship between the interviewee and Sleepy John Estes is described.

ctx.x: And who's this fellow Ham Lewis you mentioned?

Well, he come in here off of a show, and he didn't have nowhere to stay, so I let him stay with me. Me and Jab had an argument and broke up, and he got a band of his own. That's the reason he got with Sleepy John Estes. So Ham Lewis could blow the jug, and so I got him. He could blow a little better than Jab. He used to play with the Dixie Jug Blowers in Louisville, Kentucky. Used to be the Dixie Jug Blowers there, and he used to blow with them long years back.
And they're good. I like them.
